title: Post spec
description: Intent, flow and transitions for one post's internal content (post -> sections -> paragraphs). One file per post, at _journals/<journal>/posts/<folder>/spec.json, authored before the prose. It is the post's only spec: it replaces spec.md, whose Non-goals, Modalities, Open questions, Decision log, Sources and Changelog sections are carried here as fields. intent, thesis.question, thesis.claim and role are copied from the journal spec and must match it.

id.description: The post's permalink; equals the post id in the journal spec.

part.description: The id of the part this post belongs to in the journal spec.

basis.description: For a spec written after the prose: what it was reconstructed from.

intent.description: The reader outcome of the post. outcome and audience must match the journal spec; the post spec may add acceptance criteria but not remove any.

thesis.description: The post's claim (must match the journal spec) and the supporting claims its sections are responsible for.

role.description: The post's role in its part. Must equal the role recorded in the journal spec.

flow.description: The pattern that orders the sections.

sections.description: The body sections in reading order, one per second-level heading between the introduction and the conclusion.

modalities.description: The docs this spec drives beyond the main article. Empty means article only.

length.description: Optional size limits the draft is checked against.

function.description: What a section or paragraph does for the argument. One function per unit.

enumDescriptions.claim: Paragraphs step 1: states a controlling idea the following units develop.
enumDescriptions.explanation: Paragraphs step 2: says how the reader should interpret a claim.
enumDescriptions.evidence: Paragraphs step 3: facts, figures, quotations or sources that support a claim.
enumDescriptions.example: Paragraphs step 3 / 'illustration': a case that shows the claim at work.
enumDescriptions.analysis: Paragraphs step 4: explains why the evidence or example supports the claim.
enumDescriptions.definition: Defines a term the argument depends on (OSU, Functions of Paragraphs).
enumDescriptions.description: Describes a person, place, thing or state of affairs (Paragraphs 'description').
enumDescriptions.process: Explains how something works, step by step (Paragraphs 'process').
enumDescriptions.comparison: Sets alternatives side by side (OSU: comparison or contrast).
enumDescriptions.cause_effect: Explores the causes or effects of what was presented (OSU).
enumDescriptions.counterargument: States a position against the thesis fairly.
enumDescriptions.refutation: Answers a counterargument (OSU: refute a point of view).
enumDescriptions.context: (extension) sets the scene or the stakes before the argument starts.
enumDescriptions.recommendation: (extension) says what the reader should do; the author's judgement, labelled as such.
enumDescriptions.synthesis: Conclusions: shows how earlier points fit together.
enumDescriptions.transition: Moves the reader from one part of the post to another (Transitions: a transition can be an entire paragraph).

organization.description: How a paragraph's sentences are ordered (Paragraphs, 'ways to organize a paragraph').

form.description: How the unit appears on the page. Tables, lists and figures are specified like paragraphs: one controlling idea each.

evidence_item.description: One piece of support a paragraph uses. Each item must say why it is relevant: 'NONE of your examples should be left unexplained' (Paragraphs, step 4).

kind.description: 'scenario' is a fictional or illustrative case and must be labelled as such in the prose.

what.description: The item itself: the figure, the quotation, the case.

source.description: Where it comes from, with a date for company facts.

shows.description: Why this item supports the paragraph's controlling idea.

advances_thesis.description: How the unit advances the post thesis (Paragraphs: every paragraph 'clearly related to the thesis').

supports.description: The post's supporting claims this unit argues for.

paragraph.description: The smallest specified unit: one paragraph (or one table, list or figure) with exactly one controlling idea.

controlling_idea.description: The single idea that 'controls what happens in the rest of the paragraph', as a full sentence a topic sentence could state (Paragraphs). If it needs 'and' to join two ideas, it is two paragraphs.

evidence.description: Required in substance for functions evidence and example; the semantic validator enforces it.

advances_thesis.description: Optional on a paragraph: when absent, the paragraph inherits its section's advances_thesis.

transition_in.description: The link from the previous paragraph of the same section. Required on every paragraph except the first of its section.

heading.description: The heading as it should appear. A reader skimming headings alone should be able to follow the argument.

controlling_idea.description: The single idea the section establishes.

flow.description: The pattern that orders the section's paragraphs. Optional for sections of one or two paragraphs.

transition_in.description: The link from the previous section (or, for the first section, from the introduction). Required on every section.

introduction.description: How the post brings the reader in (Introductions).

bridge.description: The path from the reader's world to the topic.

from_reader_world.description: The situation the reader already recognises.

to_topic.description: The step that turns that situation into the post's question.

thesis_statement.description: Where and how the thesis is stated. It must appear in the introduction, never for the first time in the conclusion (Conclusions: the 'Sherlock Holmes' conclusion).

text.description: The thesis as the reader will meet it; may be worded more plainly than thesis.claim but must say the same thing.

placement.description: Which element carries it (for example 'KEY POINTS bullet 1 and paragraph p02').

roadmap.description: What the introduction tells the reader to expect. A reader of the introduction alone must be able to predict the sections from it (Introductions: 'Ask a friend').

kept_in.description: The sections that keep the promise.

conclusion.description: What the post leaves the reader with (Conclusions).

synthesis.description: How the sections' points fit together into something no single section says. Not a list of what each section said ('Synthesize, don't summarize').

so_what.description: Why the reader should care, answered concretely (the 'So What' game).

callback.description: The return to the introduction ('Return to the theme or themes in the introduction').

to.description: The element of the introduction that is picked up again, normally the hook.

how.description: What the reader can now see in it that they could not at the start.

hand_off.description: The link to the next post in reading order. Must agree with the next post's transition_in in the journal spec.

transition_in.description: The link from the last body section into the conclusion.
